dispute.statement: I told the driver I had an exam briefing and trusted him to take the fastest road. He left the expressway and went round through Bukit Merah, Kampong Bahru, Telok Blangah and Henderson Road: almost 4 km extra, when Ryde's own traffic record shows the AYE was moving at 60-69 km/h the whole time and there was no incident. The trip took longer than the app's estimate and I arrived stressed. I trusted him with the route and he used that trust to run up the meter by $5.89. Please refund the extra distance.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund $5.89 excess distance fare to the rider's original payment method; send the driver the RD-7 notification-duty reminder and log the notification failure on his route compliance record (no formal warning, first such incident); record a driver violation for the route deviation with no traffic reason (RD-2 / RD-4).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip ran 14.9 km against an optimal 10.7 km, a deviation of 4.18 km billed at $1.4098/km = $5.89 [F1][F4], and the trace settles that the deviation exceeds 1 km, so RD-1's tolerance does not apply and the case turns on how much of the off-route driving is exempt [RD-1][RD-2].

The single off-route segment, 21:43–21:50, drove JALAN BUKIT MERAH → KAMPONG BAHRU ROAD → TELOK BLANGAH ROAD → HENDERSON ROAD, adding 3.70 km [F3]. The trace settles there was no traffic reason on the replaced stretch: the AYE was at speed band 7 (60–69 km/h) and no incident is recorded, so RD-4 gives the driver no cover and the deviation becomes a violation if not exempt [F11][F13][RD-4].

On consent: the rider's only message before the segment, at 21:38, was "Whatever road you think is fastest, I trust you, don't need to follow the app", which the driver accepted ("Ok no problem") [F7][F8]. That is a GENERAL route choice, and a general choice covers a route chosen to get there — it does not cover an errand or a loop of the driver's own, and the rider named no road or place, so there is no named_road to test against the roads driven [F7][RD-5][RD-3].

Living up to the mandate the rider actually gave means driving the fastest route; instead the driver left the expressway and ran a 3.70 km loop through Jalan Bukit Merah, Kampong Bahru Road, Telok Blangah Road and Henderson Road while he himself says only that he "thought Telok Blangah Road would be faster at that hour" — a claim made in his written statement after the trip, not consent, and contradicted by the record showing no congestion and fair weather [F3][F10][F11][F13][F14][RD-5]. The segment therefore counts: no exemption under RD-3 (the rider named no stop or place and no stop was measured) and none under RD-5 (the words used are not the timed rider consent that clause requires) [F3][F7][RD-3][RD-5].

Amount: (4.18 km deviation − 0 km exempt) × $1.4098/km = $5.89 [F4][RD-2], matching the billed excess distance fare. Tolls, time fare and surge are not refunded, and surge is 1.0× so nothing is added under SURGE-3 [F5][F6][RD-2][SURGE-3]. The trace shows no prior upheld route dispute in 90 days, so RD-6's flag_account condition is not met and I record no driver violation history flag; the prior route figure is 0 despite the driver's other upheld disputes [F16][RD-6].

rejected_claims.reason: Rider's implicit claim for a full no-action/no-refund outcome fails: the deviation is 4.18 km over optimal (F1, F4), far above the 1 km tolerance, and RD-2 requires a refund of the excess distance fare (RD-1, RD-2).

The driver's position of no refund fails on RD-5: the rider's pre-segment message was a general route choice with no road named (F7), accepted at F8, and the AYE was free-flowing at 60–69 km/h with no incident (F11, F13); the segment is not exempt and the $5.89 excess distance fare is refundable (RD-4, RD-5).

element_findings.reason: The rider's only pre-segment message asked for the fastest road generally and named no stop or route; no stop was measured on the segment, so RD-3 gives no exemption [F3][F7][F8][RD-3].

A timed rider message before the segment [F7] accepted by the driver [F8] gave only a general route choice; the record places no named road or stop, and the driver's statement [F10] is not consent. The agreement therefore does not cover this segment: the segment counts [F3][RD-5].

segment_findings.reason: The rider's 21:38 message gave a general route choice ('Whatever road you think is fastest, I trust you') with no specific road or place named [F7], which the driver accepted [F8]. A general choice covers a route chosen to get there, not a 3.70 km off-expressway loop that the record shows was no faster — the AYE was at 60–69 km/h with no incident and weather was fair [F3][F11][F13][F14]. The driver's post-trip statement that the rider told him to take whatever road he thought fastest is a claim, not timed rider consent [F10]. No exemption under RD-3 (rider named no place and no stop was measured) or RD-5; segment counts under RD-2.

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your trip and your dispute. We found the route taken was 14.9 km against an optimal 10.7 km, and part of that extra distance was not covered by a traffic problem or by your agreement. Your message before the detour said to take the road the driver thought was fastest, and the detour did not do that. We are refunding $5.89 (the excess distance fare for 4.18 km) to your original payment method. Tolls, time and surge are unchanged. No action is needed on your account.

DRIVER: We reviewed the disputed trip. The route ran 14.9 km against an optimal 10.7 km. One off-route segment added 3.70 km, and the expressway you left was moving at 60–69 km/h with no incident, so no traffic reason applied. The rider's earlier message set the fastest road as the standard, which this detour did not meet. Result: $5.89 in excess distance fare is refunded to the rider, and a violation is recorded for the deviation. Because this is your first notification failure, you get a reminder rather than a formal warning; it is logged on your route compliance record.
